correctness.rationale: The two affine-coordinate slices prove exactly three endpoint-hypercube vertex layers, each with 2^m elements; active independent facet normals rule out missing vertex degeneracies. Conditional on the three hub-layer choices, all m leaf squared distances factor as 2+2q, 2+2q^4 or 1+2q+q^4, with hub offsets 0,1,4. Their ordered sum and diagonal correction give equation (1) identically. Fixed bounded i.i.d. squared differences have exact means 1/2, 3/2, 2 and variances 1/4, 9/4, 4; type probabilities 2/9, 2/3, 1/9 yield limits. The second largest coefficient is exactly 4m+4 in the ordered polynomial, giving 2m+2 unordered pairs. The checker enumerates 786420 ordered vertex pairs and checks integer coefficient identities up to m=100; finite evidence corroborates but is not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The complete squared Euclidean pair-distance polynomial is an intrinsically natural metric invariant of a documented infinite family. It strictly improves known global radius, diameter and f-vector information: uniformly random vertices occupy three separated macroscopic distance regimes with probabilities 2/9,2/3,1/9 and three different Gaussian fluctuation variances. The location and counts of the second-highest chord shell are additional exact geometrical information; there is no arbitrary parameter slice or ad hoc invariant. The metric must be fixed and is clearly specified.
